name: HELIO HOSTEL SAPPORO
detail: I used it for a 2-night, 3-day stay due to some business. It was my first time using it, and overall it was clean and comfortable. Pros: - Cheap prices. - There is a café and lobby on the first floor where you can relax after checkout. - Amenities are well-stocked. - Conveniently located near a convenience store and Tanukikoji shopping street. - The staff are kind. - There is a women-only shower room. - It is quiet while sleeping. → I think it is perfectly comfortable for those who just want a place to sleep! Cons: - You can't eat food in the sleeping area, so you have to move to the space on the first or fifth floor (drinks are allowed). - It is quite difficult to place a suitcase on the upper bunk of the bunk bed (the ladder is attached and hard to climb). - The bed lighting uses an orange bulb, which made it personally difficult to apply makeup. The cons are minimal, and overall it was a hotel I would like to use again.

name: The Centurion Sauna Rest & Stay Sapporo Male Only
detail: Rating: ★★★★☆ Purpose of use: Short trip Room type: Standard Cabin Upper level This was my first time using this service, and the check-in process to the guest room was very smooth. The polite response from the staff, including the female staff member at the reception, was impressive, and I was able to spend my time comfortably until checkout. The cabin was clean, and the large public bath was comfortable with a good range of amenities. I felt that the variety of baths was limited, with the sauna being the main feature. The dining options available on the food floor are plentiful. It’s good for those who have eaten well in the Sapporo and Susukino area to enjoy a drink, or for guests to indulge in food and drink at the hotel. However, the shared toilet on the cabin floor had a slight odor, and the cleaning of the cabins started earlier than checkout time at 10 AM, which is a downside. Nevertheless, I would like to use this service again if I have the opportunity to experience a break from the ordinary.

name: APA Hotel Sapporo Odori Ekimae Nishi
detail: I stayed at APA Hotel for the first time because it was affordable. From the moment I arrived, the staff were kind and attentive. The person who checked me in at the front desk was gentlemanly and helpful. I've stayed at various hotels, but this was the first time I received such considerate treatment, which left a strong impression on me. The room was efficient, and it was convenient to watch TV from the bed. It would be perfect if there were a large public bath. The bathroom was clean, and I felt it was just right for staying alone. They provided a room on a higher floor with a good view, for which I am grateful. The restaurant was also on-site, and the meals there were delicious! It was my first trip to Sapporo, and I checked out with a very good impression. I will definitely stay here again. I hope to get a room on a higher floor next time too... Thank you very much for your care.

name: Hotel Resol Trinity Sapporo
detail: There is a bus stop from the airport right in front of the hotel. The staff is very helpful. There is a hot tub with ice cream and drinks available. They provided three pillows. The bed is comfortable and it's right in front of Odori Park. It's not far from the fish market. I will definitely use the service again. It's also not far from shopping areas, which is great.

name: JR Tower Hotel Nikko Sapporo
detail: 1. I highly recommend this place for travelers who need to use public transportation. It is a transportation hub where you can easily access JR trains, city buses, subways, and various tour buses. 2. The view from the room is fantastic, and the bedding is great, making for a comfortable night's sleep. The services like pajamas, bottled water, tea, and various amenities were excellent. The room's hygiene was also good, and despite the age of the hotel, it felt very well maintained. 4. The facilities are very good. The hot springs with great views and quality water seem unique to this hotel. The lounge where you can relax after the hot spring bath is luxurious, and even the detail of providing ice cream shows their attentiveness. 5. The breakfast is delicious, and the staff is very friendly. The view from the breakfast restaurant on the 32nd floor is so beautiful that it whets your appetite on its own. 6. The friendliness and professionalism of the hotel staff are very impressive. 7. The hotel is conveniently located next to a department store and shopping mall. It’s an easy walk to the bustling district of Susukino via an above-ground road, and in winter, you can use the underground road to explore the underground shopping areas and the city without feeling like you are far from Susukino, as it's only two stops away. If you want an elegant and convenient trip in Sapporo, I highly recommend this hotel.

name: Hotel Gracery Sapporo
detail: Like most hotels in Japan, the room was just spacious enough to open one suitcase. There wasn't any major inconvenience. It could be uncomfortable if you need to open two suitcases? The hot water worked very well, and the water pressure was good; the bathroom was quite spacious. No bottled water was provided, but there was a water purifier in the hallway, so I took some for the coffee pot. The bathroom amenities included squeeze bottles of shampoo, conditioner, and body wash (which smelled good), while the lobby had toothbrushes, toothpaste, razors, skin lotion, bath salts, green tea, drip coffee bags, hair oil, etc. There were no unpleasant odors in the room's bathroom, and the sound insulation wasn't particularly bothersome. I turned up the heater a lot, but it wasn't warm because I hadn't turned it on... Everyone, please remember to turn it on! The breakfast was delicious! It was neat. You could make your own sake don, and the scrambled eggs were tasty. There were three kinds of juice, which seemed freshly squeezed, and the coffee was also good. The gown was nice; I wanted to take it with me.

name: ANA Crowne Plaza Sapporo By IHG
detail: On the final day of my one-week stay in Sapporo, I stayed at the ANA Hotel. Since I had been walking around a lot, having a bathtub was essential, and becoming a hotel member allowed for late checkout until 2 PM! Additionally, there was a Seicomart convenience store on the first floor, where I could easily buy a little ice cream after my bath. After dinner, when I was too exhausted to go out, the hotel's top-floor bar provided a great view of the nightscape along with a drink, making my stay luxurious. The facilities were somewhat old, but the cleaning was thorough, there were enough towels, and I could get only the amenities I needed at check-in from the front desk. I enjoyed coffee in my spacious room, and the bed was fluffy, allowing me to sleep soundly. I appreciated having USB ports and power outlets by the bedside. In the morning, I bought bread from the bakery on the first floor and enjoyed it in my room; the bread was delicious and made for a perfect conclusion to my last day in Sapporo, as I was able to relax. Moreover, they kindly stored my luggage after checkout. After an early dinner, I picked up my bags at the hotel and took a taxi to Sapporo Station without any stress before boarding the airplane. I definitely want to stay here again when I come back to Sapporo.

name: Hotel Plus Hostel SAPPORO
detail: The location was good, convenient for shopping, and gave an easy-to-use impression. The facilities and services were well-equipped, and the Wi-Fi could be comfortably used. The bathroom was also user-friendly, well-cleaned, and overall I had a pleasant stay. The staff's response was polite, and considering the services provided, the price felt reasonable. Regarding cleanliness, it gives the impression that while it's not perfect in every detail, it is generally well-maintained. Overall, it is a highly satisfying accommodation.

name: Ten to Ten Hostel
detail: It is great that you can walk to Sapporo Station. The bed is fluffy and comfortable to sleep on. Although it is a bunk bed, there were more reservations on the upper bunk than I expected. There was also a small rectangular outlet to plug in a charging cable next to the pillow, and a small shelf to place glasses.

name: Granbell hotel Tanuki, Sapporo
detail: It is within walking distance to downtown, you can enjoy a good bath, have a tasty breakfast, and shop well nearby. All the staff are friendly, and this is my second visit, and I was satisfied and had a good rest. The bathhouse and the entire hotel are clean and tidy. There is a parking lot, but it is 20,000 yen for one night. Nearby, there is a Time parking lot for 1,300 yen for 24 hours, so if you are bringing a car, keep that in mind (very close).
